summary: Opaque Linux binary embedding P2P WebRTC remote-control stack with QR pairing
details: The npm package ships a single ~13 MB Linux/amd64 ELF at bin/sxt with no README, no repository, no author, no source, and no scripts. Symbols in the binary show it statically links the full pion WebRTC stack (webrtc/v4, datachannel, sctp, dtls/v3, srtp/v3, stun/v3, turn/v5, ice/v4, mdns/v2, interceptor) together with coder/websocket for signaling and skip2/go-qrcode for pairing-code generation. This combination — P2P data channels, NAT traversal, WebSocket signaling, and QR-code pairing — is the technology set used by interactive remote-shell / terminal-sharing tools that give a remote peer an interactive channel into the host running the binary. The only publisher-provided pointer is package.json's license field, which links to https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, a personal account whose repository name self-describes the tool as a control channel. There is no way for an installer to audit what bin/sxt does when executed. Running the binary opens a remotely-reachable interactive channel into the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
